analysis:
Documentation-only PR. docs/provider/direct-mode.md (head lines 47-54) now says standalone `--local` preload runs an excluded shape warmup before the listener opens, and that the 5-second sweep tick warms deferred or lazily loaded engines once the server is idle. docs/reference/configuration.md (head line 413) adds the `DARKBLOOM_TTFT_SHAPE_WARMUP` env var: `0/false/no/off` disable it, `always` skips the shader-cache probe, and it is forwarded to the LaunchAgent.

No code, auth, crypto, attestation or coordinator-wire behavior changes. The patch touches no trust boundary (TB-002/TB-003/TB-007/TB-011), no key or token handling (A-003, A-008) and no App Attest authorization (A-016). The warmup is described as training no rate or counter and as an ordinary local compute step, so it does not change prompt confidentiality (A-001).

The only security-adjacent question is whether warmup could use real consumer prompt data or alter the prefix cache (T-041). The docs say it uses synthetic 128-token probes and shape cells, and they do not mention the SSD prefix cache. The implementation in ModelCalibrationPolicy.swift is not supplied. A later pass should confirm that warmup inputs are synthetic, are never donated to the encrypted SSD prefix cache or exposed via logs, and that the 20 s per-engine bound holds. This is an unverified contract, not a finding.

The documented forwarding of the env var to the LaunchAgent is an allowlist addition (LaunchAgent.passthroughEnvironment). It is only a disable/skip-probe knob, so it adds no meaningful attack surface. configuration.md base lines 1-353 were checked for conflicts with the new row and none were found. The base text does not show the LaunchAgent passthrough list, so that forwarding claim is unverified.
